# Tobit Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_003_page_001.jpg

---

**1** In the depths of my grief I wept and prayed:

**2** "Lord, you are righteous. Everything you do flows from mercy and faithfulness. Your judgments are true and just, now and always.

**3** Lord, remember me. Look at me. Do not punish me for my sins — or for the sins of my ancestors, who stumbled before you without fully knowing what they were doing.

**4** They broke your commandments, and so you handed us over — to raiders, to chains, to death — and made us a cautionary tale, a byword of shame among every nation where we were scattered.

**5** Your judgments on me now are many, and they are just. I have what I deserve — I and my whole family — because we did not keep your commands or walk honestly before you.

**6** So do what seems right to you, Lord. Give the order — take my spirit, let me go. Let me turn back to dust. It is better to die than to live like this. I have endured slander I did not earn, and the grief inside me is more than I can bear. Lord, command my release. Let me go to the eternal home. Do not turn your face from me. It is better to die than to live this way — scorned, broken, with no relief in sight."

**7** That very same day, in the city of Ecbatana in Media, something terrible was happening to a young woman named Sarah, the daughter of Raguel. One of her father's servants had turned on her with vicious words —

**8** because Sarah had been married seven times, and every one of her husbands had been killed by the demon Asmodeus before the marriage could even be consummated. The servant spat at her: "You're the one killing your husbands! Seven men, and not one of them lived long enough to call you his wife.

**9** Why do you take it out on us? Your husbands are dead — go join them! Don't you dare have children who have to live with what you are!"

**10** The words broke her. Sarah went up to her father's room at the top of the house with every intention of hanging herself. But she stopped. She thought it through. "If I die this way, people will blame my father. They'll say: 'His only daughter — and she hanged herself in despair.' I can't do that to him. I can't drag my old father's grief down into the grave. No. I won't hang myself. I will pray. I will ask God to let me die — and then at least I'll never have to hear these words again."

**11** Right then, at that hour, she knelt at the window with her hands raised toward the light and prayed:

"Blessed are you, O Lord my God, and blessed is your holy and glorious name — now and forever. Let all creation sing your praise.

**12** Lord, I am looking to you. Here I am before you.

**13** Say the word and release me from this earth. Let me hear no more reproach.

**14** You know the truth, Lord. You know I am innocent. I have never been with a man.

**15** I have never brought shame on my own name or on my father's. I am all he has — his only child — with no brother, no nephew, no family connection left for me to marry. Seven husbands. Dead. Every one of them. Why should I keep living? If you don't want to take me yet, Lord — then at least see what I'm going through. See my shame, and have mercy."

**16** At that very moment, in the same instant, the prayers of both Tobit and Sarah rose up and were heard before the throne of the great and glorious God.

**17** And Raphael was dispatched — sent out to heal them both. He would remove the white films from Tobit's eyes so the old man could see light again. And he would bring Sarah to Tobias as his wife, freeing her from the shadow of Asmodeus. It had been ordained from on high that Tobias was the one she was meant for — he had always had the prior claim, before any of the others who had come for her. At that very hour, Tobit turned away from his courtyard and went inside. And in Ecbatana, Sarah came down from the upper room.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- Verse 6: Tobit's prayer is not resignation — it is raw petition. The double request ("it is better to die") is the voice of a man at the edge. PNEUMA tries to render the emotional exhaustion and the dark logic of his despair without sentimentalizing it.
- Verse 8: "Spat at her" — not in the Greek, but the servant's words carry contempt that is almost physical. PNEUMA adds this to convey the quality of the attack.
- Verse 9: The servant's "Don't you dare have children" is an attempt to render the Greek's "let there never be seen from you son or daughter forever" as the violent curse it is.
- Verse 10: Sarah's interior monologue is the emotional center of the chapter. PNEUMA expands it slightly for modern readers, preserving every element of the Greek reasoning (suicide → shame to father → grief → alternative: prayer).
- Verse 15: "I have never been with a man" — PNEUMA makes Sarah's declaration of sexual purity direct and unambiguous, crucial for her legal and spiritual defense before God.
- Verse 16: "before the throne of the great and glorious God" — PNEUMA amplifies slightly to convey the grandeur implied by GII's unique phrase.
- Verse 17: "ordained from on high" and "prior claim" render the lot-casting concept in terms modern readers can grasp — divine Providence working through Israelite inheritance law.

*— PNEUMA*
